rationale: No spec existed, so acceptance was skipped and the run is graded low confidence; 23 blocking findings survive, none confirmed critical, and several (admin role listing, id/email mismatch, Dockerfile import chain, sslmode) are capped at major because reachability was unconfirmed. 13 candidates were dismissed as noise or handled elsewhere, nothing was deferred, and the standards audit had no coverage gap (commit-format failed, code-quality partial).

standards_review.notes: git-workflow.md requires EPMCDME-####: Description; 35 of 36 subjects conform but 'epmcdme-15435: add planning artifacts' uses a lowercase prefix and description
New coordinator.py uses bare dict/list annotations; new idp_lock.py lacks from __future__ import annotations. License headers present; Ruff not run

No concrete issue found: secrets come from env/secretKeyRef and are not logged; DB password quote_plus-encoded; sync fails closed on partial Keycloak reads; IDP lock guards at router and service layers

findings.title: Sync image build contradicts requirements-sync.txt and is unverified
findings.problem: The Dockerfile comment says the full poetry main deps are used because the minimal requirements-sync.txt fails on the import chain, yet requirements-sync.txt is added in the same change, is referenced by nothing, is unpinned, and its header says heavy stacks must not be in the sync image. The image copies only selected source directories (utils/leader_lock.py alone, rest_api/models only, no enterprise or rest_api package init files), and nothing in the diff builds the image or imports the entrypoint inside it.
findings.impact: Either a dead, misleading dependency file ships, or the image violates its stated non-goal. A missed module in the hand-picked COPY list would surface only as an ImportError at container start in the cluster. Reachability of a concrete missing import was not confirmed.
findings.recommendation: Delete or wire up requirements-sync.txt, and add a build-and-import smoke check (python -c 'import codemie.enterprise.sync.entrypoint') for Dockerfile.sync.

findings.title: CronJob renders invalid values with no required guards
findings.problem: With keycloakSync.enabled=true and the empty defaults, image renders as ':<tag>' and POSTGRES_HOST/POSTGRES_DB/KEYCLOAK_ADMIN_URL/REALM render empty; there is no `required` guard. The pod hard-mounts the ConfigMap codemie-custom-customer-config, which this chart does not create and which is not marked optional. The template fallback for the DB secret ('postgres-credentials') differs from the values.yaml default ('codemie-postgresql'), and the pod reuses the API service account with no securityContext or resource defaults.
findings.impact: A forgotten value or missing ConfigMap yields an install that succeeds and a CronJob that fails every run (ImagePullBackOff, ContainerCreating) instead of a render-time error.
findings.recommendation: Use `required` for image.repository, database.host/name and keycloak.adminUrl/adminRealm, mark the ConfigMap volume optional or document and expose keycloakSync.customerConfigMap in values.yaml, and align the secret-name defaults.

findings.title: Rollback and pause instructions are wrong or unsafe
findings.problem: The docs say to pause the CronJob by scaling replicas to 0 (CronJobs have no replicas; spec.suspend is the mechanism), mark stopping the CronJob as optional during rollback, reference IDP filter rules, sync filters and realm mappings that do not exist in this change, use realm 'codemie' where values.yaml says 'master', and copy the oauth2-proxy secret with a sed '/namespace:/d' that deletes every line containing 'namespace:'. They also tell operators to reuse the login-proxy client as the Keycloak admin client.
findings.impact: An operator who rolls back with IDP_MANAGED_ENABLED=false but leaves the CronJob running keeps having memberships removed and fields overwritten that were just made editable again; the pause instruction does not work.
findings.recommendation: Document `kubectl patch cronjob ... suspend=true`, make stopping the CronJob mandatory in rollback, remove references to non-existent filters/mappings, fix the sed command, and state the Keycloak roles the admin client needs.

findings.title: IDP lock enabled without checking the provider supports it
findings.problem: The validator forces ENABLE_USER_MANAGEMENT=True whenever IDP_MANAGED_ENABLED is set, with no provider check and no log line, while the adjacent comment still says it is only active for IDP_PROVIDER=keycloak. In enterprise/idp/dependencies.py `_accepts_idp_managed_flag` returns False for constructors taking **kwargs or with an uninspectable signature, so with an older enterprise package the flag is silently not passed to the provider.
findings.impact: With a non-Keycloak or local provider, user, project and membership mutations (including admin password change) are locked with nothing to replace them. With an older provider the API enforces the lock while the IdP provider runs unmanaged. No warning is logged in either case.
findings.recommendation: Validate IDP_PROVIDER=keycloak when IDP_MANAGED_ENABLED is set (or log a warning), log the forced ENABLE_USER_MANAGEMENT change, update the comment, and warn when the provider cannot accept idp_managed_enabled.

findings.title: Bare dict/list annotations in new module
findings.problem: code-quality.md prefers parameterized generics; the new module annotates with bare dict and list at lines 107, 129, 162, 181, 212, 302-304, 337-344, 416-418, 438-439.
findings.impact: Documented code-quality standard is not met in new code; flagged as blocking by the standards audit.
findings.recommendation: Replace with dict[str, Any], list[dict[str, Any]], list[Any] | None, dict[str, int] and similar.

findings.title: Disabled or deleted Keycloak users are never deprovisioned
findings.problem: Only enabled=true users are fetched and the coordinator can only create, update and reactivate. A user disabled or deleted in Keycloak stays is_active on the platform, and the API deactivate endpoint is locked in IDP-managed mode. Without a spec it is ambiguous whether deprovisioning is intended; treated as a blocking gap.
findings.impact: Offboarded users keep platform access indefinitely and no path remains to remove it in IDP-managed mode.
findings.recommendation: Deactivate platform users absent from a completely-read Keycloak user set (guarded by the full-read check), or state explicitly that deprovisioning is out of scope and provide an alternative path.

findings.title: batch_size not validated and user paging has no hard cap
findings.problem: _fetch_users stops only on an empty or short page and has no page cap, unlike _get_all; KEYCLOAK_SYNC_BATCH_SIZE of 0 or negative is accepted (a size of 0 makes `len(page) < batch_size` never true). A server that ignores `first` and returns full pages loops until activeDeadlineSeconds, despite the CR-011 comment claiming this is prevented.
findings.impact: A bad config value or misbehaving Keycloak produces a hung or failing job; the docs' 'users per batch' wording does not match the behaviour (all users are held in memory and committed once).
findings.recommendation: Raise on batch_size < 1, add a max-page guard that raises like _get_all, and correct the batchSize docs.

findings.title: Admin role read ignores group and composite role holders
findings.problem: Admin status comes only from /roles/{role}/users, which in Keycloak lists direct role holders and not users who hold the role through group role-mappings or composite roles.
findings.impact: Such users are computed as is_admin=False and demoted by the sync on every run. Reachability depends on how the realm assigns the admin role and was not confirmed.
findings.recommendation: Resolve effective role membership (group-inherited and composite) or document that only direct role assignment is supported and surface it in dry-run.

findings.title: Group read failures can look like empty groups
findings.problem: _group_member_ids does `self._get_all(...) or []`, so a non-list first page (None) is treated as an empty group while the snapshot is still considered complete. _subgroups also falls back to the embedded subGroups on any /children failure (500, timeout), not only a 404 on old Keycloak, and that embedded list may be empty or truncated.
findings.impact: A valid-looking snapshot with missing members makes the sync strip real memberships.
findings.recommendation: Make _group_member_ids raise when _get_all returns None, and fall back in _subgroups only on a 404; otherwise re-raise so the snapshot becomes None.

findings.title: Dry-run report under-reports and reconciliation is N+1
findings.problem: In dry-run a new user is counted as created but _create_user returns None, so that user's membership additions and removals are never previewed. The project-admin flag update bypasses the repository and is not counted in SyncResult or the dry-run summary. _reconcile_memberships issues one aget_by_name per existing membership plus one per Keycloak project for every user, inside a 300s deadline.
findings.impact: The dry-run the docs tell operators to validate before going live omits changes the live run will make, and the per-user query volume risks hitting the activeDeadlineSeconds kill, which discards all uncommitted work.
findings.recommendation: Preview memberships for would-be-created users, count admin-flag updates in SyncResult, and batch the application lookups.

findings.title: User matched by email with a different id is overwritten
findings.problem: When no row has the Keycloak id, the user is looked up by email; a match with a different id is updated as the same person, including is_admin overwritten from Keycloak, with no id-mismatch check. Created users take the Keycloak id as primary key.
findings.impact: A reused or reassigned email could attach a different Keycloak identity to an existing platform account and its memberships. Reachability not confirmed.
findings.recommendation: Detect an id mismatch on the email match and skip or flag it with a warning instead of updating.

findings.title: No revocation when Keycloak names no project
findings.problem: _reconcile_user_memberships returns early when the applications attribute and both group maps are empty (CR-013 by design). A user removed from their last Keycloak group or project keeps every platform membership indefinitely. The intent is ambiguous without a spec, but it contradicts IDP-managed source-of-truth semantics.
findings.impact: Project access is never revoked for users who lose their last assignment in Keycloak, and the locked API offers no alternative.
findings.recommendation: When snapshot.groups is complete, treat an empty set as authoritative for previously synced users (or document and decide the intended revocation behaviour).

findings.title: applications_admin projects ignored when not otherwise listed
findings.problem: kc_project_ids is attr_projects | group_projects | group_admin_projects, while kc_admin_project_ids also includes the applications_admin attribute. A project present only in applications_admin never gets a membership, and a user whose only data is applications_admin does not pass the early-return guard.
findings.impact: The admin assignment is silently ignored, and the two admin sources (attribute vs group) behave inconsistently.
findings.recommendation: Include the applications_admin projects in kc_project_ids and in the early-return guard.

findings.title: Counters incremented before the savepoint can roll back
findings.problem: _sync_user adds users_created/updated/reactivated to result inside begin_nested() before the membership step. If membership reconciliation raises, the savepoint rolls back the user write but the counters stay, and the user is also counted as a failure.
findings.impact: The sync_complete summary reports changes that did not persist.
findings.recommendation: Accumulate counts locally and add them to result only after the savepoint block succeeds.

findings.title: Total per-user failure still reports ok and exits 0
findings.problem: run() returns status='ok' regardless of result.user_failures, and a Keycloak outage or empty /users result returns 'skipped'; entrypoint exits non-zero only for 'error'. ttlSecondsAfterFinished=600 with a 10 minute schedule also removes failed jobs and their logs quickly.
findings.impact: A persistently broken sync looks like success to Kubernetes and monitoring.
findings.recommendation: Return an error status (non-zero exit) when user_failures > 0 or the Keycloak read fails, and keep failed job history long enough to inspect.

findings.title: Engine never disposed and PG_URL query params unsupported
findings.problem: get_async_session builds a new engine on each call and never disposes it. The PG_URL rewrite only swaps the driver prefix, so a libpq-style query such as ?sslmode=require or a postgres:// scheme is passed through to asyncpg, which does not accept it.
findings.impact: Connection failure at start for common managed-Postgres URLs, and unclosed pool connections at exit. Whether the deployment's PG_URL carries such parameters was not confirmed.
findings.recommendation: Handle the postgres:// scheme, strip or translate sslmode, and `await engine.dispose()` in a finally block.

findings.title: _validate_env cannot detect a missing POSTGRES_HOST
findings.problem: A variable passes if either getattr(config, VAR) or os.environ[VAR] is truthy, and config.POSTGRES_HOST defaults to 'localhost', so the check never fires for it; the comment claiming it must differ from the default is not implemented.
findings.impact: A missing database host is not caught: the sync connects to localhost and fails late instead of failing fast.
findings.recommendation: Check os.environ for the required variables (or compare against the default) so an unset POSTGRES_HOST exits with SystemExit(1).

findings.title: KEYCLOAK_SYNC_ENABLED is never read
findings.problem: KEYCLOAK_SYNC_ENABLED and KEYCLOAK_SYNC_SCHEDULE are added to Config, but main() never checks the flag. The Helm template hard-codes KEYCLOAK_SYNC_ENABLED=true, and the docs tell operators to set it on the CronJob as a switch.
findings.impact: Setting it to false does not disable anything; operators are given a false off switch and the sync still writes to the database.
findings.recommendation: Exit early with an info log when KEYCLOAK_SYNC_ENABLED is false, or remove the dead flag from config, chart and docs.

findings.title: New module lacks from __future__ import annotations
findings.problem: code-quality.md requires `from __future__ import annotations` in new modules; idp_lock.py does not have it.
findings.impact: Documented code-quality standard is not met; flagged as blocking by the standards audit.
findings.recommendation: Add `from __future__ import annotations` after the module docstring.

findings.title: Dry-run create and admin-flag branches are untested
findings.problem: The dry-run tests only cover an existing user with a profile change and stale or new memberships. Neither the _create_user dry-run early return nor the 'not dry_run' guard around the project-admin flag mutation runs in any test.
findings.impact: Removing either guard would make a dry-run sync insert users or flip project-admin flags (the session is committed at the end of run()) while every test still passes.
findings.recommendation: Add a dry-run test with an unknown user asserting acreate is not awaited and users_created == 1, and one with a differing is_project_admin asserting no mutation or flush.

findings.title: Entrypoint tests never check run() arguments or _validate_env
findings.problem: The main() tests patch _validate_env and coordinator.run and assert only no-raise or SystemExit(1); they never inspect the arguments passed to run(), and _validate_env is never executed by any test.
findings.impact: If main() stopped forwarding dry_run or batch_size, the documented dry-run-first step would write to the database with no failing test; _validate_env could be deleted or inverted unnoticed.
findings.recommendation: Assert mock_run.assert_awaited_once_with(batch_size=..., dry_run=...) and add tests that call _validate_env() with missing variables expecting SystemExit(1).

findings.title: Info test cannot detect a dropped idp_managed_enabled
findings.problem: test_app_info_includes_idp_managed_enabled sets the config False and asserts False, which equals the InfoResponse default, and accepts either camelCase or snake_case via `or`. Several guard tests in test_user_management_router_idp_guard.py only check that the dependency is wired, not that requests are rejected, and the file has orphaned section headers.
findings.impact: If the router stopped forwarding config.IDP_MANAGED_ENABLED, /v1/info would always report false and the UI would not learn the mutations are locked, with all tests passing.
findings.recommendation: Set IDP_MANAGED_ENABLED=True and assert data['idpManagedEnabled'] is True (parametrize both values), and add rejection-behaviour assertions for the guard tests.

findings.title: Commit subject violates EPMCDME-####: format
findings.problem: The commit 'epmcdme-15435: add planning artifacts' in the review range uses a lowercase ticket prefix and lowercase description, against git-workflow.md.
findings.impact: The commit-format standard is violated by a commit in the range, which blocks the workflow.
findings.recommendation: Reword to 'EPMCDME-15435: Add planning artifacts' or ensure the squash commit uses that format.
